text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- President Guntis Ulmanis, acting Prime Minister Anatolijs Gorbunovs and Army Commander Juris Dalbins and other officials are to visit the district of Zaube in central Latvia, where the electricity has been cut off due to heavy snow.

- The hearing of the case of the five Latvian pilots arrested for arms smuggling in India has been postponed from January 3 to January 20. According to sources, the delay may be due either to the judge falling ill or because he has been replaced.

- From January 1 two kinds of sick-lists, A and B, have been introduced in Latvia. The first, effective for the first 13 days of sick-leave, will be paid by the employer but the second, effective after the 15th day, will be paid by the government.
- The merger between Savings Bank and the Union Baltic Bank in Riga is to take place by the start of February after being approved by the Bank of Latvia.
- The World Bank and Parex bank signed a contract on distributing a $35 million World Bank credit line through Parex.
